mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In rising rate regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day average (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% while PAYEMS increases by more than 5,000 in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is <0.3, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during neutral labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above the prior month's level accompanied by a rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) predicts a near-term upward revision in GDP growth expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month growth > 2% and HOUST month-over-month increase > 5%
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 tested instances where both INDPRO and HOUST meet the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in energy prices (not directly observable in the catalog but proxy via CPIAUCSL with energy component assumed) and a simultaneous rise in raw material costs (indirectly via GDPC1) creates a supply shock that depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month decrease of 3% while GDPC1 month-over-month increase of 2%
failure_condition: In 50 tested events matching the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in FEDFUNDS, it indicates a labor market softening that lowers discount rates, thereby supporting equity valuations and generating positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months and FEDFUNDS <= 4% during the same period
failure_condition: Over 10 such softening regimes, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than during tight labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly job openings (PAYEMS) of over 20,000 accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a labor market cooling that reduces business optimism and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month decrease > 20,000 while UNRATE month-over-month increase > 0.1%
failure_condition: In 30 tested events with the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in consumer spending (HOUST) by more than 10% above the prior month's trend is interpreted as a strong demand signal, which elevates growth forecasts and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month growth rate > 10% above prior month's growth rate
failure_condition: Across 40 such events, the 5-day forward return is not significantly higher than during steady demand (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and raw material costs (GDPC1) by at least 2% each month indicate a supply-side softening that raises uncertainty and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decrease >= 2% and GDPC1 month-over-month decrease >= 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 40 tested contraction regimes, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically lower than during expansion (p > 0.1).
